summary: The snapshot deadline test no longer fails with Errno::ENOENT when a busy machine delays its fixture. It now records the child process ids Open3 starts instead of reading a pid file the child writes after it starts.

intent.why: `test_snapshot_deadline_reaps_the_active_native_child` read a `pid` file its Ruby fixture writes only after it starts, under a 2 s deadline.
intent.user_impact: None for Shaka users; the change only affects this repository's tests.
intent.root_cause: On a loaded machine the deadline killed the fixture before it wrote the file, so the test read a missing file.
intent.safe_because: Only tests change; the test also fails if the deadline waits for the child instead of killing it.
intent.scope: The test now records the pids `Open3` spawns through a shared `test/support/open3_spawns.rb` helper, which the transport deadline test from #1209 also uses. The first read now hangs, so exactly one child starts. The fixture no longer writes the file.

checks: The old assertions with a 0.1 s deadline raised `Errno::ENOENT`; the new test passes with the same deadline.
`ruby -Itest ... -n /deadline/` passed 30 of 30 runs under 120 busy shell loops at load average about 370.
With `DeliveryGitHub#terminate` stubbed out, the test fails: `Expected 60.19 to be < 30`.
verification.not_verified: The unchanged test passed 20 of 20 runs under 120 busy loops, so the race was reproduced only with a shortened deadline.

checkpoint.audience: Shaka maintainers running the test suite on busy machines.
checkpoint.repair_history: Not recorded in the frozen case.
